reason: The neutral locator (p. 447, prenatal dexamethasone effect on adult offspring acoustic startle response) does not uniquely distinguish among the overall two-way ANOVA main effect across diurnal phases ("DEX: F(1,70) = 7.520; P = 0.008"), the nested-litter light-phase comparison ("[F(1,28) = 5.963; P = 0.021]"), and the non-significant nested-litter dark-phase comparison ("[F(1,28) = 3.462; P = 0.073]"). Although the authors state that the study "replicates our earlier ﬁnding of increased basal startle in blood sampled animals, prenatally exposed to DEX and tested during light phase [9]" and "replicated our earlier ﬁndings in a new strain and laboratory," the unresolved target test prevents confirming an effect-specific replication verdict without relying on numeric coincidence.
